According to some historians, after the fall of the Western Roman Empire and transition into the Middle Ages, it's said that the Franks contributed the most in defining the Middle Ages as a whole and continued to shape most of Europe up until the end of the Middle Ages. How true is this and what did they do to define the era?

message.content: Franks defined the era via conquest, faith, plus governance. That dynasty rebuilt western lands with new codes and empire. Yet other groups, like Vikings, also shaped a medieval age.

- Clovis I converted to Catholic Christianity (496), aligning Frankish power with the Church
- The Carolingian Renaissance under Charlemagne (crowned Emperor 800) reestablished imperial authority in the West
